topic: Classification of Organisms Based on Risk of Extinction
key_concepts: High biodiversity helps populations overcome adverse conditions.
A species is a group of organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
Biodiversity includes all living organisms and environmental aspects within an ecosystem.
Extinction occurs when no known living individuals of a species remain.
Conservation status classifies a species based on its risk of extinction.
Endemic species are restricted geographically to a particular area.
Threatened species are likely to go extinct if nothing is done to protect them.
The IUCN Red List assesses global extinction risk for animals, fungi, and plants.
The IUCN Red List is updated at least twice each year and informs conservation policy.
